anomalies.observed: Q1 pin 3 is tied to GND while JP1 pin 1 is tied to VCC_OUT (J2 pin 2) and JP1 pin 3 is tied to Q1 pin 1. With the jumper in position 1-3 (as drawn) or 2-3, Q1 sits between VCC_OUT (or VCC) and GND — i.e. in parallel with the fan — so when Q1 turns on (PWM high) the supply rail is shorted to ground instead of powering the fan.
anomalies.expected: For switched fan power the MOSFET must be in series with the fan: a high-side PMOS with source to VCC and drain to VCC_OUT (J2 pin 2), or a low-side NMOS with drain to J2 pin 1 (fan ground) and source to GND while J2 pin 2 is tied directly to VCC. As drawn, Q1 pin 3 should connect to VCC_OUT, not GND.

evidence.quote: J2 pin 2 'VCC_OUT' → JP1 pin 1; JP1 pin 2 → 'VCC'; JP1 pin 3 → Q1 pin 1; Q1 pin 3 → 'GND' (page 1, sheet /)

anomalies.impact: In the switched (2-wire) jumper positions the fan never receives power and Q1 shorts VCC_OUT/VCC to GND whenever PWM is high, risking damage to the regulator and MOSFET; only the bypass position (JP1 1-2, 4-wire mode) works.

parsed.summary: The fan power-switching stage is mis-wired: Q1 is placed in parallel with the fan (between VCC_OUT and GND via JP1) instead of in series, so turning Q1 on shorts the supply to ground rather than driving the fan.
